blocks.text: PROFESSIONAL PROFILE

Data Scientist and Staff AI Engineer with a background in statistics, machine learning, and production systems. Develop ML models, LLM applications, and AI agents, from defining the problem and testing an approach to deployment and ongoing evaluation.

Work spans anomaly detection, application security, data pipelines, and the infrastructure needed to run models reliably. Research how code, dependencies, permissions, and exposed features can create exploitable paths through a system.
Registered PhD Researcher at the University of Greenwich and creator of Chagu. Study security and accountability in agentic AI using anomaly detection, provenance graphs, and blockchain.

Security Beyond Chagu
Data science for application security and attack-path analysis
Research how attackers can reach and influence software through its dependencies, code, and exposed features.

Study how ML, LLMs, and agents can support static application security testing (SAST), software composition analysis (SCA), infrastructure-as-code (IaC) analysis, and software bill of materials (SBOM) enrichment.
Investigate whether attack patterns, code reachability, and execution context can reduce false alerts from isolated rule matches and help reviewers focus on exploitable issues.
Research deterministic attack-path discovery across code, dependencies, configuration, and permissions. Record the conditions each path requires and the evidence needed to validate it.
Map inputs from contact and lead forms, issue reports, support tickets, uploads, APIs, webhooks, chatbots, and agents. Trace how those inputs can reach internal data or actions.
Study malicious and vulnerable packages, transitive dependencies, installation scripts, dependency hijacking, typosquatting, protestware, and maintainer history.
Assess how SBOMs, attestations, Sigstore, in-toto, and SLSA can help verify where software came from and how it was built.
Explore persistent memory and retrieval using retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and knowledge graphs, with batch and streaming pipelines for data and context used by LLMs and agents.
Study graph learning, sequence models, and anomaly detection for dependency exploitability, CI/CD drift, and unusual log behavior.
Research developer copilots that explain findings, suggest secure fixes and pull requests, generate policies as code, and explain misconfigurations. Examine MCP integrations and VibeCoding workflows.

Define reference test sets and evaluation measures: precision and recall at fixed alert budgets, attack-path coverage, developer acceptance, time to signal, and cost per scan. Use repeatable tests and feedback to check detection quality.
Example scenarios include Log4j exploitation, Shai-Hulud package compromise, malicious issue titles, poisoned CRM submissions, and instructions hidden in support tickets.
